title: November 12 — GN-XOR, self-writing one-wire loops, window controls, jitter and shared phase
summary: Eight related repositories: GN-XOR, KultaaVaiKatinkultaa, KultaaVaiKatinkultaaOpus, GoldOpus, GoldSol, GoldGemini, PhaseLockedPredictiveCoding and MuistoVaihde. Synchronous native GN27 mismatch works, and one unsigned error pulse feeds a ring that both writes and erases. But a ~25-line checkerboard-free window unit reproduces 255/255 pattern learning, while native-specific behavior is so far faults and an unexploited clock. K integration and global temporal alignment work in defined synthetic settings, not as new AI principles or measured transformer accelerators.

nodes.claim: 5×7 coprime-ring conjunction learner with a 35-entry explicit weight table and a 35-slot joint-memory ring; independent V2 directed-transition replay loop.
nodes.survived: All 35 A/B phase meetings occur in one cycle; trained A-only cues reconstruct taught B patterns. V2 replay from seed P emits A@7, B@14, END@21 after observed P→A→B→END teaching.
nodes.killed: Designed Hebbian-like table and transition lookup, not a native GN mechanism; identical cues linked to different episodes recall their union. Shared tick, no self-organized learning of temporal routes.
nodes.era: November 12: nonlinear memory and phase controls

nodes.claim: Three unchanged V27 native units implement a synchronous event-presence XOR through a non-monotone setpoint response, and an eight-relay seeded prediction ring detects mismatches.
nodes.survived: Native truth table 4/4 at hand-selected −4.5 input weights; omitted or unexpected beat produces expected error spikes at the comparison node.
nodes.killed: One-tick offset breaks both-present cancellation. The initial ring is seeded; no learning or general Boolean identity detection is demonstrated.
nodes.era: November 12: nonlinear memory and phase controls

nodes.claim: Sol's unchanged GN27 signed innovation/omission and single unsigned XOR feedback into an eight-unit event-memory ring.
nodes.survived: Native 11-unit signed circuit performs write/erase; simpler one-wire configuration and window control both eventually learn 255/255 nonempty synchronized eight-slot rhythms. Native isolated c=1 clock ~59 ticks.
nodes.killed: Hand-selected timing/weights; some source events merge; ±1 timing jitter breaks silence; nine-relay native leak persists even with damp-branch forcing; no performance advantage over small control.
nodes.era: November 12: nonlinear memory and phase controls

nodes.claim: Opus's independent native GN27 audit and checkerboard-free window-model reduction of the one-wire mismatch-feedback ring.
nodes.survived: 255/255 nonempty eight-slot rhythms learned on both. In 33-case stress, native one-wire ring memory exact 31/33 vs native signed pair 22/33; abstract window ring exact 33/33 relative to emitted source. Abstract unit ~17× faster.
nodes.killed: Source emitted correct requested beat stream in only 20/33 cases because close pulses merge; native-specific ring leak is a fault. XOR and toggle/delay-line logic are known; checkerboard is unnecessary for core behavior.
nodes.era: November 12: nonlinear memory and phase controls

nodes.claim: Public ten-neuron reduced-window tapping looper with a K-consecutive-tick integration gate for human rhythm jitter.
nodes.survived: At correctly spaced hops, tested K=2j+1 handles ±j timing jitter across 255/255 eight-slot rhythms (K5 at ±2, K7 at ±3). Error events rewrite changed rhythms and become silent.
nodes.killed: Not native checkerboard GN27; K window is conventional debouncing/coincidence integration. Tempo is tied to supplied click track and there is no compute/energy advantage over simple digital memory.
nodes.era: November 12: nonlinear memory and phase controls

nodes.claim: Independent attempt to identify native GN27 slow-state advantage via signal_in jitter rescue and two history-state ablations.
nodes.survived: No consistent jitter benefit across 12 tested settings; 12 of 336 identical probes differed after conditioning, all at two-tick recovery, restored by swapping four-tick pipeline (12/12), not the 50-tick variance buffer (0/12).
nodes.killed: Negative finite test only, not proof against all GN applications; reducing error spikes alone did not mean fewer missed or extra predicted beats.
nodes.era: November 12: nonlinear memory and phase controls

nodes.claim: Visual 64×64 grayscale scene represented by four bit planes/pixel, each a logical delay stream updated by reduced-window one-wire mismatch feedback.
nodes.survived: 16,384 logical bit streams with period-16 memory amount to 262,144 stored logical bits, displaying world, ring replay and error.
nodes.killed: Ordinary buffer-backed software update, not 16,384 original GN27 instances, hardware efficiency proof or novel video-background algorithm.
nodes.era: November 12: nonlinear memory and phase controls

nodes.claim: Global three-candidate temporal phase selection by Hamming distance before comparing many stored binary streams to the current known-period world.
nodes.survived: On synthetic frozen 16-frame templates with ±1 independent global timing shifts, 128/128 phase selections correct; fixed-phase 77,071 false mismatch bits vs hub zero (no intruders); with intruders 768/768 true local changes caught, versus per-pixel best phase 741/768.
nodes.killed: Only temporal frame-phase selection, not camera spatial warp or learned PLL; ±2 offsets, independent regional timings and phase-shaped novelty produce failures; no transformer speedup measured.

edges.why: GN-XOR copies V27 unchanged core and tests its native three-unit synchronous XOR.
Sol extends the native comparator to signed discrepancy and error-written circulating memory.
Opus reuses the original V27 code and creates a reduced window control.
Independently made Sol/Opus circuits are later cross-tested; conceptual reconciliation rather than an inherited code fork.
The abstract window control is extended with K-tick integration and a browser rhythm looper.
GoldSol extends Sol's native one-wire audit with original signal_in and history perturbations.
Reduced band-pass XOR/toggle rule scales to buffer-backed logical pixel-stream rings, not GN27 replicas.
The reduced ring-buffer comparison is extended with shared temporal phase search and novelty controls.
Conceptual circular-memory influence only; MuistoVaihde explicitly engineers independent CRT/Hebbian/transition mechanisms.

motifs.title: One endogenous error signal toggles memory; the native geometry is dispensable
motifs.description: For synchronized binary events, e=w XOR r and r_next=r XOR e=w. One non-monotonic comparator, one writeback wire, and an event loop work; an abstract band window reproduces the central results. Classic T flip-flop/delay-line algebra, not demonstrated novelty.

motifs.title: Local temporal tolerance and a shared temporal address are distinct mechanisms
motifs.description: GoldOpus integrates coincidence windows; the phase hub chooses among t±1 remembered templates for many streams. Both work under specified synthetic timing tests; neither proves spatial camera-motion compensation or hardware speedup.

motifs.title: Shared clocking organizes memory but does not learn context for free
motifs.description: MuistoVaihde uses 5×7 CRT addresses and explicit association weights, with episode collision; shared global template phase is an address chosen by exhaustive comparison, not a persistent learned complex main state.
